title: Jamie Ritchie ruled out Scotland duty as Franco Smith delivers injury update
article_text:
Franco Smith has confirmed that Jamie Ritchie has sustained a knee injury against the Lions which will rule him out of the Nations Championship.

The 30-year-old was released from Scotland camp to make his home debut for Glasgow Warriors but disaster struck after eight minutes.

Ritchie needed medical attention on the pitch and limped off to be replaced by Ally Miller in a devastating blow.

Ritchie experienced injury issues at Perpignan last season and Glasgow have been patient with integrating him this season and he only debuted against Benetton last weekend.

It’s too early for a full diagnosis on the former Scotland captain’s issue but Warriors head coach Smith is almost certain it’s a Medial collateral ligament (MCL). That will sideline Ritchie for a minimum of 4-6 weeks, which will rule him out the full Nations Championship.

“It's an MCL injury,” said Smith. “We hope that. He's walking around obviously with it being honest. We hope that it's not that serious.

“Obviously, it's bad luck for him and it deprives an opportunity from him. He's just come back from his injury and he's got such a good influence in the club at the moment. So I hope that it's not serious and he'll recover.

“But there's now four weeks.  If he's going to recover earlier, fantastic. And Scotland will benefit from it. But there's now four weeks without games for us, so that will take a big chunk of that. Maybe we'll get him back when we need him most.

Pressed on the timeframe for Ritchie’s return, Smith replied: “Yes, it's four to six. It depends. It could be a strain. We don't know the seriousness of it.

“Like I said, I do not want to do the doctor's job here. And don't make a diagnosis unnecessarily. So currently we're going to wait and on Monday we'll have a better idea. But the original thoughts are more or less there.”

Glasgow survived a second-half fightback from the Lions to record a bonus-point to preserve their unbeaten start to the season.

The Warriors were miles from their best without a host of key internationals and Smith was just delighted to get the win.

“I'm excited about the way that we played,” said Smith. “The fact that we deprived them so much from creating, they ended up scoring an all-try, which is uncharacteristically from them.I'm excited about the way that we played.

“Obviously, we're going to look back and say we've allowed them to score tries, but they are a team that scores tries.We had very, very good moments. Yes, there's a patch where they played well and we made mistakes, which we tried to avoid. But overall, I'm really chuffed with the result.”

title: Wales complete Japan double to end WXV on a high
article_text:
Wales completed a WXV double over Japan with a comfortable 29-5 victory in Kumagaya City.

Wing Nel Metcalfe and hooker Moe Nagaoka exchanged tries in the opening 15 minutes before hooker Kelsey Jones and wing Amy Williams added to Wales' first-half haul.

In-form prop Sisilia Tuipulotu crossed after the break before Williams added her second in a rare move from the backs.

Wales were then reduced to 13 players with replacements Keira Bevan and Hannah Dallavalle both shown yellow cards, but dug defensively deep to keep the hosts out in the dying minutes.

Wales finish the Global Series with three wins, their only defeat coming against USA. It marks a complete transformation for Sean Lynn's side, who prior to the South Africa game had gone nine Tests without a win.

The Sakura Fifteen, meanwhile, are still waiting for their first victory since May and a first under head coach Toshizumi Kitagawa.

Wales, who ground out a 17-0 win in the opening Test, had the better of the early exchanges.

They were rewarded with the opening try after Japan's loose goalline drop-out, which co-captain Alex Callender thundered up deep into the 22.

Tuipulotu then came close, before the ball was shipped to Metcalfe to finish in the corner. Lleucu George, preferred at 10 this week to Bevan, added the conversion.

The hosts then enjoyed a spell of pressure thanks to Wales' indiscipline and bagged their first try of the double header with hooker Nagaoka touching down from the maul.

Wales were back among the tries 10 minutes later with George's kick putting the defence under pressure and Lisa Neumann winning the turnover.

Wales rightly backed their line-out with Jones touching down for her second in as many games. George was again on target from the tee to extend Wales' lead.

Despite improved conditions this week, the visiting backline looked a little disjointed, but the maul was dominant and Japan could do little to stop it from gaining ground before Seren Lockwood found Williams in space on the wing.

Japan's indiscipline proved costly in the second half, with Jennifer Nduka paying the price for an accumulation of penalties with a yellow card.

It paved the way for Wales to cross for the try bonus-point, with Tuipulotu proving unstoppable from a metre out.

Wales continued to play through the forwards, with Callender working tirelessly in her new position of eight this week.

The backs eventually got in the action and it came from a huge Callender pass out wide to Neumann who fed the pacy Williams for her second run in of the evening.

Both sides emptied their bench soon after, and while Wales' replacements proved the difference last weekend, it had the opposite effect this week, with the experienced Bevan and Dallavalle both shown yellow cards as the game entered its final 10 minutes.

Bevan had been penalised when Wales had been on a warning, while Dallavalle, making her first appearance in the competition, was given her marching orders for a blatant hair pull.

Japan threw everything at Wales in the dying moments, but could not take advantage of their numbers and it was fitting that Callender came up with the crucial turnover.

Wales co-captain Kate Williams said: "We played some exciting attacking rugby, especially in that first-half to get a few of our tries.

"I'm really proud of the set piece as well. I think what slowed down our momentum was our discipline and we let Japan back into the game a little bit in that second-half.

"But really proud of the defensive effort that we showed, especially with those two yellow cards. There was some real grit and determination behind that."

Wales: Neumann; N Metcalfe, Cox, Keight, A Williams; George, Lockwood, Pyrs, K Jones, Tuipulotu, B Metcalfe, Crabb, K Williams (co-capt), Lewis, Callender (co-capt).

Replacements: Reardon, Davies, E Jones, Aiono, Evans, Dallavalle, Bevan, De Vera.

title: Zverev thrashes GB's Fery to reach Vienna semis
article_text:
Alexander Zverev marked his rise to world number one with a dominant victory over Britain's Arthur Fery to reach the semi-finals of the Vienna Open.

The German top seed, who is set to replace Jannik Sinner at the summit of the men's rankings, needed just 58 minutes to secure a comprehensive 6-0 6-2 win.

Fery did not look at his best throughout the encounter after receiving treatment on his leg near the end of his last-16 win over Lorenzo Musetti on Thursday.

The match was a repeat of the pair's Wimbledon semi-final this summer, which Zverev won in straight sets to end Fery's remarkable run.

"I think Arthur is a bit of a different opponent than I had yesterday. He doesn't have the same firepower, but he plays tactically extremely well," said Zverev.

"I know the score was 6-0 6-2, but he should not put himself down too much. It is his first year on the Tour and he is doing amazing things."

Like at Wimbledon, Fery upset the odds to reach the last eight in Vienna by beating former world number five Musetti, but the 24-year-old was outclassed by Zverev.

Zverev dropped only six points on serve in the match, while bringing up nine break points against Fery, converting five of them.

The German is aiming for his third title this year after winning the French Open and US Open.

He has taken advantage of injuries to Carlos Alcaraz and Sinner this year to leapfrog them in the rankings, becoming the second German to reach the top of the men's game after Boris Becker in 1991.

Zverev will face Australian fifth seed Alex de Minaur or Italy's Matteo Berrettini in the last four.

In the other semi-final, Spanish second seed Alcaraz will face Russian third seed Daniil Medvedev.

Seven-time Grand Slam-winner Alcaraz beat American seventh seed Tommy Paul 6-4 7-6 (7-2) in his quarter-final.

Medvedev triumphed over France's Adrian Mannarino 6-2 6-3 in his last-eight tie - a victory which seals the 30-year-old's place in the season-ending ATP Finals.

It will be Medvedev's seventh time appearing at the finals as he joins the already-qualified Zverev, Alcaraz and Ben Shelton.

At the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo, world number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from her quarter-final tie against Leylah Fernandez with a neck injury.

Rybakina's withdrawal comes one day after she secured the year-end women's singles number one ranking.

Fernandez, who received a walkover, will face Russia's Kamilla Rakhimova in the last-four.

title: JSW Sports expands global commercial footprint with Hong Kong Sixes partnerships
article_text:
JSW Sports has brought a portfolio of marquee brands on board for the ongoing 2026 Hong Kong Sixes, strengthening the tournament’s commercial proposition as the company expands its presence in the international sports market.

The partnership portfolio includes Kajaria, ARM, Boldfit, CREX, Mastercoin and UE Group, among other brands.

The development follows JSW Sports’ appointment as the exclusive commercial partner of Cricket Hong Kong, China (CHKC) in September 2026. Under the agreement, the company is responsible for driving the tournament’s commercial and marketing strategy, including securing sponsorship partnerships and creating opportunities for brands to engage with cricket audiences.

Commenting on the partnerships, Himanshu Sharma, Head of Sales, JSW Sports, said, “Taking our commercial capabilities to an international sporting property is an important milestone for JSW Sports. The Hong Kong Sixes presents a distinctive proposition for brands, combining the appeal of cricket with a fast-paced format that lends itself to engaging fan experiences. The response from our partners reflects the opportunities that international sporting platforms can offer brands looking to expand their engagement with sports audiences. Our focus remains on building partnerships that deliver meaningful value for brands while strengthening the commercial ecosystem around sport.”

The association marks JSW Sports’ first commercial partnership with an international sporting property. The company is leveraging its experience in franchise operations, sports marketing, athlete management and sponsorship development to strengthen the tournament’s commercial ecosystem.

The 2026 edition began on October 30 and runs until November 1 at the Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground in Hong Kong. The tournament features 12 national teams competing in its distinctive six-a-side format, offering brands access to a fast-paced sporting property with an established international following.

title: Arizona partners with Carvana for jersey patch sponsorship
article_text:
Arizona men's and women's basketball jerseys will have a Carvana patch on the right shoulder, and a Monster Energy patch on the left shoulder.

The University of Arizona and Arizona-based online car retailer Carvana announced a partnership that designates Carvana as the exclusive auto partner of Arizona athletics and the official jersey patch sponsor for Wildcats men’s and women’s basketball.

The deal makes Carvana the first jersey patch partner in school history and will extend beyond athletics to create broader connections between Carvana and the University of Arizona, according to the university’s press release.

“We are pleased to announce this transformative partnership between Arizona Athletics and Carvana,” Arizona athletic director Desireé Reed-Francois said. “Carvana has deep Arizona roots and shares our commitment to innovation, competitive excellence and community engagement. The depth of this partnership showcases the power of the Wildcats brand and creates impactful opportunities for our men’s and women’s basketball student-athletes. We appreciate everyone who worked together to bring this to life.”

Proud to officially announce @Carvana as exclusive auto partner, official jersey patch partner of @ArizonaMBB & @ArizonaWBB, & an official University of Arizona partner! pic.twitter.com/9jD26onSok

The partnership will also include in-venue branding at McKale Center, digital and social content, radio and ESPN+ inventory, game sponsorships, fan activations and hospitality opportunities. Examples include a season-long social media series of short- and mid-form storytelling on both programs and the integration of Carvana-sponsored Wildcats basketball alumni reunions.

Carvana will also work with select men’s and women’s basketball players on Name, Image and Likeness initiatives.

“Arizona men’s basketball is a premium brand built on our people, our tradition and the standard we strive to uphold every day,” men’s basketball head coach Tommy Lloyd said. “Carvana shares that commitment to people and excellence, and we are grateful for their meaningful investment in our program. We’re excited to welcome them to our family and to serve the best fans in the country together.”

All Big 12 Conference football and basketball programs now have a Monster Energy patch on their jerseys after the energy drink company partnered with the conference ahead of the 2026 season. Arizona’s Carvana patch will be stitched on the right shoulder above the Nike logo, while the Monster Energy-Big 12 patch will be on the left shoulder.

title: Women's Rugby Union: WXV Global Series - WXV Japan v Wales - 31 October 2026
Argentina Roster for Ireland Comes with Returning Hero
article_text:
Los Pumas head coach Felipe Contepomi has finalized Argentina’s first roster for the Nations Championship. His 33-man roster will travel to Dublin to prepare Argentina’s opening match of November on Friday, November 06 against Ireland.

The naming of the roster comes with the notable inclusion of a returning hero. After missing out on international duty in both 2024 and 2026, and only playing for Argentina in July 2025, veteran Facundo Isa is back. Isa has been called-up in place of the injured Santiago Grondona.

The other alterations to the roster were already made following the original announcement of the training camp. Loose head prop Thomas Gallo and utility back Santiago Carreras were both named only to be ruled out with injuries. They join the aforementioned Santiago Grondona plus Ignacio Ruiz and Joaquín Oviedo on the unavailable list. Of them Gallo, Carreras and Oviedo are out with longterm injuries.

Missing Pumas has been a theme for Argentina throughout 2026. The lack of a global season and the decision of New Zealand and South Africa to not compete in the Rugby Championship in 2026 meant adjustments to which Felipe Contepomi took action to blood players, reward players with recalls, and attempt numerous new combinations.

There are missing players who will be in action but for the Argentina XV rather than Los Pumas. Tight head prop Pedro Delgado and flanker Benjamín Grondona are two cases in point. Another is rookie Pumas flanker Juan Penoucos.

There are also players who featured this year but have not been selected. Examples of veterans include Matías Alemanno, Gonzalo Bertranou and Matías Moroni. The latter of these two players has 99 test caps for Argentina.

A notable non-selection is that of Franco Molina. The second-rower debuted in 2024 and has since been a mainstay in Contepomi selections. The November roster is the first without him with veteran Tomás Lavanini back instead. This also comes with no place for Franco Carrera and Luciano Asevedo. Both are uncapped second-rowers yet both have trained with the roster this year.

Further cases include Nicolás Roger who started against Australia in Mendoza and Francisco Coria Marchetti who featured in July. Finally, outside backs Santiago Pernas and Tobías Wade miss out. Both players were in consideration to play against South Africa and Australia earlier this year.

title: ‘No such thing as No. 1 by default’: Rolex Paris Masters hails Zverev before Paris ceremony
article_text:
‘No such thing as No. 1 by default’: Rolex Paris Masters director hails Zverev before Paris ceremony

Alexander Zverev (No. 1) starts the Rolex Paris Masters as world No. 1, and tournament director Cédric Pioline rejected any idea that he got there by default. Pioline cited the German’s 2022 Roland-Garros injury and his diabetes, and the tournament will mark his rise with an ATP ceremony.

Alexander Zverev will start the Rolex Paris Masters as world No. 1, and tournament director Cédric Pioline will not hear a word about luck. Asked on Friday whether the German was a worthy No. 1 or a No. 1 by default, Pioline shut the question down.

“There’s no such thing as being world No. 1 by default,” Pioline said. “Maybe he had opportunities, and he knew how to seize them (winning Roland-Garros and the US Open). I think he’s a beautiful No. 1, because we have to remember certain things in his story.”

Pioline pointed to the 2022 Roland-Garros semifinal, when Zverev left Court Philippe-Chatrier in a wheelchair after injuring his ankle against Rafael Nadal. “He left Roland-Garros’ Centre Court in a wheelchair when he was playing almost his best tennis. He was, to say the least, hanging with Rafael Nadal,” he said. “And he plays as a diabetic, which is an incredible message of hope for everyone. Whatever the level, everyone can be a champion in their own way.”

“So yes, he’s a beautiful No. 1, with two Grand Slam titles this year, a final and a semifinal,” Pioline added. “No, he’s not No. 1 by default at all.”

The tournament will celebrate Zverev’s rise with a ceremony organized with the ATP. “It’s the tradition, always at the tournament that follows the accession,” Pioline said at the draw.

Zverev, the 2024 champion in Paris, is the top seed. He will play the winner of Lorenzo Musetti and Hubert Hurkacz after a first-round bye. Jannik Sinner, last year’s champion, has withdrawn after ending his season, and Felix Auger-Aliassime, the runner-up, has also withdrawn. Zverev’s projected path runs through Learner Tien (No. 15), then Novak Djokovic (No. 10) or Alex de Minaur (No. 8) in the quarterfinals. Carlos Alcaraz (No. 2) is at the other end of the draw.

title: Errani and Paolini secure final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells
article_text:
- Singles and doubles draw will be made at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden on Tuesday November 3 at 3 p.m. which will be streamed live on TikTok

The WTA on Saturday announced Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini have secured the final qualification position for the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells, setting the stage for the world's best doubles team to compete for the prestigious WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy.

Errani and Paolini are set to make their third consecutive appearance at the WTA Finals and complete the doubles lineup, which features Taylor Townsend & Katerina Siniakova, Gabriela Dabrowski & Luisa Stefani, Guo Hanyu & Kristina Mladenovic, Cristina Bucsa & Nicole Melichar-Martinez, Hsieh Su-Wei & Jelena Ostapenko, Ellen Perez & Demi Schuurs and Elise Mertens & Zhang Shuai.

With both fields now set, the singles and doubles draws will be made at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden on Tuesday November 3 at 3 p.m. (PST) which will be streamed live on TikTok as part of a new global content partnership.

Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini are celebrating their third qualification for the WTA Finals as a team following an impressive campaign on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.

Their performances at the WTA 1000 level were key to securing their place. They finished runners-up at the Miami Open presented by Itaú in addition to three semifinal runs at the BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells), Qatar TotalEnergies Open (Doha) and the Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open. They will also contest the title match at the WTA 500 Toray Pan Pacific Open (Tokyo) on Sunday.

Both players have experience in singles at the WTA Finals, with Errani qualifying from 2013-14 and Paolini in 2024 and 2025.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20). This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivaled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment, and culture.

Get your tickets here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

title: HYLO Open: Hoo/Lai’s Form Holds
article_text:
Hoo Pang Ron and Lai Pei Jing continued to perform impressively as they made the last four of the HYLO Open 2026 – a fifth semifinal from their last six tournaments.

The Malaysian world No.24 duo, runners-up at last week’s YONEX French Open, overcame Hong Kong China’s Chan Yin Chak/Ng Tsz Yau 21-17 21-17, and will next take on world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue.

The top half will see fifth seeds Amri Syahnawi/Nita Violina Marwah against Jesper Toft/Amalie Magelund.

Malaysia had further good news, with new pairing Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King surging into the semifinals. The Arctic Open champions got the better of Chiu Hsiang Chieh/Wang Chi-Lin 21-16 21-17 and next face Christian Faust Kjaer/Rasmus Kjaer, while the other semifinal will feature Julien Maio/William Villeger against Ben Lane/Sean Vendy.

In women’s singles, world No.53 Anmol Kharb upstaged compatriot and No.6 seed Unnati Hooda after a hard-fought battle. Kharb held off Hooda in 68 minutes, 21-17 18-21 21-16 to earn a semifinal against yet another compatriot, second seed Pusarla V Sindhu, who had a comfortable quarterfinal win over Amalie Schulz, 21-12 21-10.

In men’s singles, Jonatan Christie made his first semifinal since the Indonesia Open in June, overcoming Kodai Naraoka 21-8 18-21 21-11. The Indonesian faces top seed Anders Antonsen, while the other semifinal will see Lakshya Sen against Toma Junior Popov.

Sen shook off a series of below-par performances to make his first semifinal since the All England in March, coming from behind to beat Kalle Koljonen 14-21 21-17 21-13.

title: Cobolli Reveals Injury Diagnosis, Plans to Play Paris Masters with ATP Finals Spot on the Line
article_text:
Flavio Cobolli has provided a positive update on the injury that forced him to retire from his second-round match against Matteo Berrettini in Vienna on Thursday.

The 24-year-old Italian, who is bidding to qualify for the Nitto ATP Finals for the first time, retired in tears while trailing his compatriot 5-2 in the opening set.

It was a gripping scenario, with injured Cobolli breaking down in tears after retiring the match. The Italian was consoled at his chair by compatriot and fellow Roman Matteo Berrettini, who knows a thing or two about having his best moments sabotaged by injuries.

After Cobolli left the court, Berrettini opened up about his friend.

“I’m so sorry for him. I’ve been there many times, maybe too many times,” Berrettini said. “That’s why I got emotional. I know how tough it can be. I know how much he wants to be in Turin, and the last thing that you want is getting an injury a few weeks before. But hopefully it’s not going to be anything too serious.”

On Friday, Cobolli took to Instagram to reveal the results of medical tests and confirm his intention to compete at next week’s Paris Masters.

“Today I underwent medical tests, which revealed a minor muscle strain,” Cobolli wrote. “I will travel to Paris on Saturday and do everything possible to play in the tournament.”

Cobolli, currently sixth in the Race to Turin, is hoping to secure one of the four remaining singles berths at the ATP Finals. Next week’s Paris Masters represents the final opportunity for players to earn qualification points.

After Thursday’s retirement, Cobolli explained that his tears were not caused by pain, but by emotion, stress and disappointment at having to abandon the match.

For now, the Italian remains hopeful of competing in Paris, where he will attempt to put the finishing touches on a breakthrough season and qualify for his first trip to the ATP Finals. Italian fans, saddened by Jannik Sinner’s early withdrawal from the event, will no doubt be elated if Cobolli comes up good.

He is slated to face either Arthur Gea or a qualifier in his second-round match in Paris, after a bye.

title: Yamaguchi eyes Korea Open title as Ahn Se-young considers rest
article_text:
"world No. 2" Yamaguchi Akane (29, Japan) could this be a golden opportunity for a title? If only Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) decides not to participate in the Korea Open, it would effectively be a clean sweep.

From Nov. 3 to 8, the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) will be held in Yeosu, Jeollanam-do. Although it is lower than Super 1000·Super 750 events, it is the highest-tier BWF World Tour tournament held in Korea.

The draw has already been released. In the first round, Ahn Se-young will face world No. 38 Kaloyana Nalbantova (Bulgaria). If she wins there, she will meet the winner of the match between Karupathevan Letsana (Malaysia·world No. 27) and Tonratchae Sain (Thailand·world No. 68) in the round of 16.

From the quarterfinals, a Korea-Japan matchup is highly possible. In the round of 16 she could meet Japan's Kungi Riko (world No. 20), and in the semifinals she could face "Japan's badminton idol" Miyazaki Tomoka (world No. 7). Akechi Hina (world No. 17), who created a semifinal surprise at the French Open, is also among the candidates. The final is likely to be a showdown between Ahn Se-young and Yamaguchi.

However, Ahn Se-young's participation has not yet been confirmed. She has entered, but considering accumulated fatigue, she plans to check her condition thoroughly before making a final decision.

Ahn Se-young has been on a punishing schedule, winning consecutive titles at the Denmark Open and the French Open within a week. In the Denmark Open final she also twisted her right foot and felt Achilles tendon pain.

As a result, there has been insufficient time to recover. Ahn Se-young showed signs of fatigue throughout the French Open. After the quarterfinal she admitted, "I am so grateful to be able to play. I plan not to worry too much about my condition when I compete, but it is very tiring."

After winning the title, she directly mentioned whether she would play in the Korea Open. Ahn Se-young said after returning home, "I will rest and continue my recovery routine. Then I will decide whether to play in the Korea Open or rest more." On her way back through Incheon Airport she said, "I think I need some time to regroup now," and added, "I will carefully check my condition and consider whether to participate."

For now, Ahn Se-young has also entered the Kumamoto Masters (Super 500) to be held in Kumamoto, Japan, from Nov. 10. Given her repeated emphasis on the need to rest, it seems likely she will take a break.

This is great news for Yamaguchi and the other entrants. Ahn Se-young boasts an overwhelming record this season of 66 wins and 1 loss, a 98.5% win rate. She has already claimed 10 titles. Among Chinese fans there is even a joke that "other players come to tournaments to try to win, but Ahn Se-young just comes to stamp her attendance (for winning)."

If Ahn Se-young also competes in the Korea Open and wins, she could claim up to 13 titles in 2026. Even excluding the Korea Open, she seems on track to achieve the historic single-season 12 singles titles no one has ever achieved. Last year she recorded 11 titles, matching Japan's men's singles legend Momota Kenta.

The player watching Ahn Se-young's participation most closely is second-ranked Yamaguchi. With China's Wang Zhiyi (world No. 3), Chen Yufei (world No. 4) and Han Yue (world No. 11) all withdrawing, if only Ahn Se-young is absent, Yamaguchi could make a clean sweep.

In particular, Yamaguchi is suffering a 10-match losing streak against Ahn Se-young. She bowed out to Ahn Se-young in the finals at both the 2026 Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games and the Denmark Open.

As a result, since winning the China Open in July, which Ahn Se-young missed due to injury, Yamaguchi has not reached the top once. For Yamaguchi, when Ahn Se-young is absent it is a critical opportunity to add another title.

title: PV Sindhu Reaches Hylo Open Semifinals, Faces Anmol Kharb Next
article_text:
Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu defeated Germany's Amalie Schulz to reach the Hylo Open semifinals. She will face compatriot Anmol Kharb, ensuring an Indian finalist.

Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu continued her strong run at the Hylo Open Super 500 badminton tournament, booking her place in the women’s singles semifinals with a comfortable win over Germany’s Amalie Schulz on Friday.

The former world champion needed just 27 minutes to register a 21-12, 21-10 victory in the quarterfinal. Sindhu controlled the match from the start and gave Schulz little opportunity to make a comeback. She won 42 of the 64 points played and also recorded a six-point winning streak twice during the contest.

Sindhu made a strong start in the opening game, building an early advantage before closing it out 21-12. She carried the momentum into the second game, maintaining control of the rallies to seal a convincing straight-game win.

The Indian will now face compatriot Anmol Kharb in the semifinals, ensuring that India will have a representative in the women’s singles final.

Anmol booked her place in the last four after defeating sixth seed Unnati Hooda in a closely fought three-game contest. The match lasted one hour and eight minutes, with Anmol eventually securing a 21-17, 18-21, 21-16 victory.

The upcoming semifinal will be an all-Indian affair, with both players looking to secure a place in the title clash. Sindhu, who recently finished runner-up at the French Open, will be hoping to continue her run and add another final appearance to her season. Anmol, meanwhile, will look to cause an upset and reach the final.

PV Sindhu secured a comfortable straight-game victory over Germany's Amalie Schulz with a score of 21-12, 21-10 in just 27 minutes to reach the semifinals.

title: Defending champion Yamashita maintains her lead after 3 rounds at LPGA Malaysia
Fritz advances to Basel SFs after his Live Race rival Fils retires
'We're just unbreakable': Red Roses respond emphatically to Canada defeats
article_text:
Meg Jones and John Mitchell cut very different figures from those we had seen over the previous fortnight.

After consecutive defeats to Canada, the captain and head coach of the Red Roses saw a comprehensive reaction against a USA Women’s Eagles team that came into the contest on a five-game winning streak.

By full-time at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, the Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 champions had beaten their hosts 55-12 and ended their WXV Global Series campaign on a high.

Recalled wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald scored four tries as England denied the Eagles sustained possession and prevented their combative back row from establishing a rhythm.

For an England team that were bruised by back-to-back losses against Canada, it was the kind of result that can give them confidence going into a six-month hiatus from Test rugby.

“We wanted to impose ourselves on the USA,” Jones said at full-time. “They came off the back of some good wins, so we knew they had momentum. We had to stop that and that’s what we did.

“When we got into it we started keeping the ball, being patient and had good control. Everyone was a threat to the line. We became unstoppable and I think that’s where the tries came from.

“Off the back of two losses, we just wanted to learn and we’ll continue to learn. We’ve got so much feedback from this tour.

“We’re going to review it like we always do, reflect, and see where we can keep growing because I know there’s so much growth in this team.

“We’re hungry to be better and to perform better. We’re just unbreakable at this point, but we need to keep pushing and growing.”

It was England’s attack that truly shone at Sports Illustrated Stadium, although the defensive efforts of Morwenna Talling, Sadia Kabeya and Lilli Ives Campion were equally as impressive.

By full-time the world champions had made 21 line breaks to the USA’s zero. Moloney-MacDonald’s quartet rightly grabbed the headlines, but it was the all-round package that the team’s head coach was most satisfied with.

“We played tonight,” Mitchell said. “We attacked, we controlled them rather than them controlling us. Some of the PAC4 [Pacific Four Series] teams like to be possession based from deep.

“Sometimes we feed teams when we don’t need to. We backed both sides of attack and we took control from there.

“We encouraged the ambition as well. There weren’t too many times we were reckless tonight. We probably got more patient as the game wore on which was pleasing.”

title: Jones challenges Red Roses to keep rivals guessing
article_text:
England are aiming to expand their attack in order to stay at the head of rugby's world order, says Red Roses captain Meg Jones.

Their four-year, 41-match unbeaten run was ended by a pair of defeats by Canada earlier this month, while New Zealand threatened victory at Allianz Stadium last month, only to be undone by Zoe Harrison's final-play try.

For so long the runaway leaders at the top of the world rankings, England could even have dropped to third with a combination of a 15-point defeat against the United States on Friday and a New Zealand win over France on Saturday.

That never looked likely as the Red Roses ran in nine tries in a 55-12 victory over the USA in New Jersey, but Jones says competition is becoming more fierce at the top of the game.

"Teams are getting better, that's the nature of it," Jones said.

"It happened in the men's game, it's happened in the women's game, and we've just got to start being probably more unpredictable.

"We've learned loads on this tour, and gained so much feedback from where we want to keep growing, getting better and keep pushing."

Jones said the win over the United States - with tries from players in the front row, back row, midfield and back three - was an example of the multiple threats they want to pose rivals.

"We played the game that we love to play, which is front-foot ball, attacking well, everyone an option, our props running through the middle," added Jones.

"I think there is hunger inside of us, that always keeps us ticking and keeps us at the top level. You can't be satisfied.

"I don't think you can stand still when you're playing competitive sport, so we're constantly striving to grow and be better."

England, who won the Rugby World Cup in 2025, will attempt to lift a ninth successive Women's Six Nations next spring. They take on Wales in their tournament opener on 10 April.

title: Leicester dominate Bristol to go top of the Prem
article_text:
Leicester took maximum points to go top of the Prem before the rest of the weekend fixtures with a 22-16 win away at Bristol.

Tries from Freddie Steward and Adam Radwan put Tigers in the driving seat after a sublime score from Louis Rees-Zammit had given Bristol an early lead.

Ollie Hassell-Collins extended Leicester's advantage to 17-7 after the break and while James Williams' two penalties closed the gap, Jamie Blamire drove over for the visitors' fourth to all-but seal victory.

But with Billy Searle missing three conversions, Leicester were not as far clear as they could have been and a third penalty from Williams closed the gap to six points to give Bristol hope in the final minutes.

Yet the hosts had to settle for a single losing bonus point as the Tigers did enough to see out the match and leapfrog Gloucester at the summit, with the Cherry and Whites set to play Northampton on Saturday (17:30 GMT).

Both sides came into the game evenly matched with three wins apiece before the autumn international break, and it was the hosts who struck first through a world-class Rees-Zammit try.

The Welsh wing side-stepped his way free and then skipped out of a tackle to run clear and dive under the posts for his fifth Prem try of the season.

Leicester responded, stealing possession to attack on the counter and Searle neatly kicked the ball out wide, where Tigers had numbers, for Steward to score in the corner on his 100th Prem start.

There were chances for more tries at either end as Fitz Harding was held up over the line for Bristol, while the excellent Ollie Chessum got the ball down for Leicester, but it was chalked off for a knock-on beforehand.

Rees-Zammit came inches away from doubling his tally as he shrugged his way out of a tackle and chased down his own chip, only for Tom Whiteley to expertly deny him.

But the momentum shift came just after the half-hour mark when Bristol indiscipline saw them down to 13 thanks to two high tackles in three minutes, with Matias Moroni and Tom Jordan sent to the bin.

With space open everywhere Tigers capitalised and Radwan sprinted sublimely from nowhere to dot down a kick that caught Bristol napping.

After spilling a catch before half-time that would have seen him score, Hassell-Collins got his try the other side of the break, this time easily collecting Searle's crossfield kick in acres of space to stretch the lead to 17-7.

Williams' penalty narrowed the gap and his second eventually brought Bristol within four points with 20 minutes to go.

But Leicester struck again to add the bonus-point score as Blamire walked over at the back of a driving maul.

Still, three missed conversions meant Leicester were not yet home and dry and Williams' third penalty with seven minutes to go set up a tense finale, but Leicester held firm to end the first block of Prem games on a high.

"We generally believed that we could win this game but, ultimately, we couldn't apply enough pressure.

"We did some great stuff on defence, turned ball over, put the ball up, but the lineout we lost all momentum - our game really thrives on building pressure on the other team and getting scoreboard pressure and we certainly had opportunities.

"We end up losing the game by six points, two tries were conceded with 13 men, that made it difficult.

"When you're playing a team like Leicester you need scoreboard pressure and line-out pressure and we couldn't do either. But that doesn't take away from the effort the boys put in."

"Good, gritty win against a good team in a difficult place to come. Really proud of the guys, some frustrations at the end, spoke to Ches [Ollie Chessum] afterwards because I thought we could have iced it earlier which is a sign that the team is in a great place.

"Really proud of what we've done - we've had three games in 12 days again. Really proud of the team, 10 guys away at the start of the week, no excuses we just got on with it.

"I'm really pleased with what the group is putting out, not just on game day but also during the week and in training."

Bristol: Jordan; Rees-Zammit. Moroni, Williams, Ibitoye; MacGinty, Randall; Genge, Oghre, Kloska; Rubiolo, Batley, Luatua, Harding (c), Ivanishvili.

Replacements: Gwilliam, Woolmore, Chawatama, Caulfield, Owen, Marmion, Bates, Grondona.

Leicester: Steward; Radwan, Kata, Bailey, Hassell-Collins; Searle, Whiteley; Van der Flier; Blamire, Heyes; Henderson, Chessum (c), Wainwright, Carnduff, Cracknell.

Replacements: Moli, Vunipola, Hurd, Stooke, Moro, Van Poortvliet, Wand, Hamer-Webb.

title: Alex de Minaur hits career milestone in Vienna to book semi-final date with Zverev
article_text:
Alex de Minaur has enjoyed a landmark 350th tour-level win of his career at the Vienna Open, downing an old rival to set up a semi-final date with the world No 1-elect Alexander Zverev.

Australia’s main man defeated Matteo Berrettini, the Italian he’s had plenty of trouble with down the years, for the second successive year in the quarter-final of the ATP 500 event at the Wiener Stadthalle.

Not only did his 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 triumph set “Demon” up for a third duel in just over a month with Zverev on Saturday but it boosted his bid to reach the season-ending men’s championship, the ATP Finals, which still lies in the balance.

World No 10 de Minaur found a way to draw first blood in a tight first stanza after saving a set point at 5-6, going on to take control of the tiebreak when the Italian, almost criminally, plonked a simple put-away into the net.

De Minaur crucially saved a couple of break points at the start of the next set and cashed in by himself breaking Berrettini for the first time in the next game when the Italian produced an embarrassing air-shot when faced with a straightforward smash.

From there, there was no way back for the world No 48 as de Minaur raced to victory in an hour and three-quarters to reach the semis of the Austrian indoor hard-court event for the third-straight year.

It all came off the back of, statistically, the equal-best serving display by de Minaur all season, getting in 71% of his first serves, as he actually out-aced the boom-serving Berrettini 5-4.

“That’s been an emphasis as of late, and I do feel like I’ve got in a good rhythm on serve and feel like I’m confident with what I’m doing,” said de Minaur.

“I maybe didn’t serve as well as I would have liked to at the start of the week, but today was a great serving display from me, and you know, hopefully I can keep it going.”

It all helped him become the ninth Australian man to reach the 350 match-win landmark after Lleyton Hewitt (616), John Alexander (591), Rod Laver (576), John Newcombe (568), Ken Rosewall (546), Phil Dent (414), Tony Roche (364) and Pat Rafter (358).

But earlier, Zverev, who recently lost to de Minaur in the Laver Cup and defeated him in Shanghai, gave a glimpse of the searing form which has him set to be enthroned as world No 1 on Monday as he powered through his quarter-final against British Wimbledon hero Arthur Fery, 6-0 6-2, in just under an hour.

“Yeah, 100 per cent, that’s the aim,” said de Minaur, pondering his latest chance to beat Zverev for the first time in an individual, rather than team, tournament.

“That’s the types of matches that you want to be playing, against the best in the world – and right now he’s the best in the world. So I’m excited for that. Another battle.”

If de Minaur beats Zverev, he’ll move back into the eighth and last qualifying spot to reach the ATP Finals for a third-straight year, with only the Paris Masters still to come as a qualifying event before the Turin end-of-season showpiece.

Earlier on Friday (Saturday AEDT), Daniil Medvedev secured his place at the Finals for the seventh time by outplaying French veteran Adrian Mannarino 6-2 6-3, setting up a last-four clash with world No 3 Carlos Alcaraz, who beat American Tommy Paul 6-4 7-6 (7-2).

title: Arthur Fils suffers ‘heartbreaking’ injury blow ahead of Paris Masters and ATP Finals
article_text:
Arthur Fils has suffered a worrying injury blow as he was forced to retire during his quarter-final match with Taylor Fritz at the 2026 Swiss Indoors.

The world No 8 retired due to an injury when trailing 2-6, 0-2 against 13th-ranked Fritz at the ATP 500 tournament in Basel.

After falling 2-5 behind in the opening set, a concerned-looking Fils left the court to receive treatment after a lengthy discussion with the trainer.

The injury appeared to surface early in the match, and it is a real concern after Fils’ 2025 season was cut short by a stress fracture in his back.

It is unclear whether Fils will be fit to compete at next week’s Paris Masters, or at next month’s ATP Finals — which he is in a strong position to qualify for.

Speaking on Tennis TV after commentating on the match, Naomi Cavaday said: “It’s such a shame; it’s been a spectacular 2026 for Arthur Fils.

“But it’s a back problem that means he just cannot compete. Miles away from feeling good enough here, and with Taylor Fritz at the other end of the court, [he] just had absolutely no chance.

“Well, we just hope that it is not a long-term injury, and that it’ll just be a few days… he can get himself back in action. Maybe back for Paris, but definitely back for Turin if he does confirm his spot there.

“It’s always really tough. Of course, six months out with the initial back stress fracture, you’ve gotta feel like it’s sensible that he doesn’t put it through anything unnecessary.”

Former ATP Tour player Gilles Muller confirmed Tennis TV had received information that Fils had “felt fine before the match.”

“It’s a bit heartbreaking. We saw yesterday [Flavio] Cobolli [retiring] in Vienna, now today Fils here in Basel,” Muller said.

“Just gotta hope it’s nothing serious. I think he made the right choice not to force it too much.

“We also have confirmation from our reporter on site that his team didn’t know what was going on — he felt fine before the match.

“But yeah, something must have happened there in the beginning of the [first] set. It didn’t look good. You could definitely see that he was not moving okay, he was low on energy, as well.”

title: Bernasconi Headlines Argentina XV Roster to face England A
article_text:
The Argentina XV roster is locked and loaded for the upcoming international assignment. The Argentine national Men’s next-of-XV will take on England A in an uncapped match in Bath, England on Friday, November 06.

The battle is an opportunity for players from both teams to play for possible call-ups to the test match arena. Both England and Argentina will play four capped test matches during the November Internationals as part of the 2026 Nations Championship.

The Argentina XV trained together for four days at Hindú Club in Buenos Aires. With that over, head coach, and former Puma, Álvaro Galindo has now confirmed a 27-man roster to travel to Bath. His roster is headlined by Bernardo Bernasconi (Benetton) but the hooker is far from being the only capped Puma.

Bernasconi is joined by Pedro Delgado (Harlequins), Benjamín Grondona (Bristol Bears), as well as capped players based in Argentina, namely the trio of and Nicolás D’Amorim, Juan Penoucas, and Santiago Pernas.

Bernasconi, Delgado and Grondona are part of a healthy contingent of players based in Europe. Galindo has also selected Matías Medrano (Benetton), Gael Galván (Agen), Juan Segundo Martín Montilla (Clermont) and Tobías Wade (Zebre Parma).

title: WTA issue response as tennis star stopped from paying tribute to Spain train crash victims
article_text:
The WTA Tour has issued a statement after Spanish tennis star Kaitlin Quevedo was 'stopped' from paying tribute to victims of the train disaster in Urda. It emerged that the world No. 86 was told she could not wear a black ribbon on her kit during a match at the Guangzhou Open, where she is now in the semi-finals. In contrast, Spain's Rafael Jodar was allowed to wear a black ribbon during his match against Valentin Vacherot at the Swiss Indoors, an ATP 500 event in Basel, earlier this week.

Quevedo was reportedly told she could not wear a similar ribbon for her quarter-final clash with Jil Teichmann. According to Marca, WTA officials told the 20-year-old that a black ribbon was prohibited.

The WTA has a policy restricting the "display of a symbol or slogan that is associated with, or intended to be associated with, a charity, cause, movement, or political party". But the women's tennis tour has now confirmed that it conducted an "internal review" ahead of Quevedo's next match against Lilli Tagger.

A WTA spokesperson told Express Sport: "Under the WTA's Symbols and Slogans Policy, displaying symbols on court is subject to specific requirements. Following internal review of this matter, we are speaking directly with Kaitlin about her wish to pay tribute ahead of her next match.

"We extend our heartfelt condolences to those who have lost loved ones in the train collisions in Spain. Our thoughts are with them, those injured and everyone affected by this tragedy."

According to Marca, the world No. 83 will be allowed to wear a ribbon during her next match. Quevedo also paid tribute to victims of the train crash on social media. "Still shocked by all that happened in Toledo. All my love to the victims' families, to the injured and affected by the train accident," she wrote.

Rafael Nadal and Carlos Alcaraz are among those who have also paid tribute. Nadal wrote: "I am following with great concern and sadness the tragic train accident in Toledo. I want to send a very big hug to all the families who have lost their loved ones. It is hard to find words in moments like these. All my affection and much strength also to the injured people. From the heart, I hope they recover soon."

At least 69 people were killed when a high-speed train crashed into the back of a stationary train near Urda, in Toledo, on Wednesday morning. Spain began a three-day period of national mourning on Thursday.

title: Aaron Tai-Roy King continue march in Europe, reach Hylo Open semis
article_text:
After defeating top-seeded Indonesians Sabar Karyaman Gutama-Reza Pahlevi Isfahani yesterday, they just took 30 minutes to knockout Taiwan’s world No 15 duo Chiu Hsiang Chieh-Wang Chi Lin 21-16, 21-17 in the last eight match at the Saarlandhalle Indoor Arena in Saarbrücken last night.

The world No 74 pair, who lifted the World Tour Super 750 Arctic Open title in their first tournament together in Finland earlier this month, will meet 26th-ranked Danish pair Christian Faust Kjaer-Rasmus Kjaer in the last four.

Aaron Tai-Roy King have the edge on paper as they had beaten the Danish pair in the semi-final at the Arctic Open in straight games.

The Aaron Tai-Roy King partnership has seen a meteoric rise in world ranking, moving up 276 spots from world No 350 in just four weeks of playing together. They are the most successful experimental pair being tried out by the Badminton Association of Malaysia in preparation for the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

Also in the semi-finals are Malaysia’s world No 24 mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing who will face world No 3 from France, Thom Gicquel-Delphine Delrue.

This is the fifth semi-final appearance at a World Tour championships in five months for Pang Ron-Pei Jing, from the 10 tournaments the independent duo have played since being paired together.

title: Turin Update: De Minaur Draws Closer, Reaching Vienna Semis
article_text:
Alex de Minaur is very much in the running in the Race to Turin standings, but he has his work cut out for him.

The Aussie earned much-needed points on Friday, taking out Matteo Berrettini, 7-6(4), 6-2, and he will face top-seeded Alexander Zverev on Saturday in Vienna with another 130 points on the line.

De Minaur would pass Rafael Jodar and move into eighth place in the standings if he can defeat Zverev – but the German holds a 9-4 edge in their lifetime head-to-head.

De Minaur and Taylor Fritz are still chasing points this weekend. Daniil Medvedev qualified on Friday with his win over Adrian Mannarino in Vienna, while Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe, Rafael Jodar and Novak Djokovic are all out and resting up for Paris.

title: Vienna Open: Alexander Zverev repeats Wimbledon victory over Arthur Fery as he progresses to semi-finals
article_text:
Alexander Zverev repeated his Wimbledon victory over Britain's Arthur Fery in the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

Fery's dream run at the All England Club this summer came to an end against Zverev in the semi-finals and the German was ruthless again, eliminating Fery in two quick sets.

Fery was outclassed by the top seed at the event, losing 6-0 6-2.

Reigning French Open and US Open champion Zverev is set to replace Jannik Sinner as world No 1 on Monday.

The 29-year-old, who will become the second German man to top the rankings after Boris Becker in 1991, hit 19 winners as he breezed through in just 59 minutes.

Zverev revealed he had struggled to sleep on Thursday night after securing his rise above Sinner in the global standings by beating Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor in the last 16.

He will face fifth seed Alex de Minaur, who beat Matteo Berrettini 7-6 (7-4) 6-2, in his 12th semi-final of the year.

"I definitely felt good," Zverev said in his on-court interview. "I think Arthur is a bit of a different opponent than I had yesterday, he doesn't have the same firepower but he plays tactically extremely well and he's extremely fast.

"I feel like when I have the ball on the racket like that it's just a good day for me. He has the score 6-0 6-2 but he shouldn't put himself down too much, he's 35 in the world, it's his first full year on tour, and he's doing amazing things.

"For him, I hope he keeps his head up and continues the work he's doing."

Daniil Medvedev secured a place at the season-ending ATP Finals for the seventh time after overwhelming Adrian Mannarino 6-2 6-3 to also reach the Vienna Open semi-finals.

The 30-year-old Russian, who missed out on the season finale last year after qualifying every year from 2019 to 2024, joins Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton in the eight-man field.

Sinner has also qualified but will not compete due to injury, leaving four places still available.

Medvedev has enjoyed a resurgent season in which he has surpassed the 50-win mark for the first time since 2023 and claimed four titles.

Medvedev took control early against Mannarino with a break of serve and eased through the opening set.

The former US Open champion broke again at 3-3 in the second set and closed out the match with another break.

Medvedev will next face Alcaraz, who defeated Tommy Paul 6-4 7-6 (7-2).

Roussin-Bouchard Tied for Second in Malaysia, Chasing First LPGA Win
article_text:
Jennifer Meyer is the Manager of Digital Operations. Jennifer has worked with the LPGA for more than a decade, working with the LPGA and Epson Tours to manage, develop, maintain, and update website content.

France’s Pauline Roussin-Bouchard put herself in contention for a career-defining breakthrough Saturday, firing a 5-under-par 67 in the third round of the Maybank Championship to sit two shots off the lead.

The 26-year-old stands tied for second place at 16-under 200 through 54 holes alongside People’s Republic of China's Yan Liu, trailing defending champion and leader Miyu Yamashita by two strokes. The total marks Roussin-Bouchard's lowest 54-hole score on the LPGA Tour, eclipsing her previous best of 204 set at the 2022 LPGA Drive On Championship. Roussin-Bouchard delivered a balanced performance on Saturday, hitting 9 of 14 fairways and 14 of 18 greens in regulation while needing just 27 putts.

"I can definitely feel it's the third round in the heat, and also like, I don't know, there was a bit more action on my end, a bit more bogeys," Roussin-Bouchard said. "I don't mind it if it means more birdies like I was saying yesterday, but overall same mindset and trying to like keep my thoughts together, and if they start wandering, just bring them back to the right place."

Experience will be key as she chases the lead during Sunday's final round. Having been in contention on tour before, Roussin-Bouchard noted that past high-pressure situations have prepared her for the moment.

"Well, I've definitely learned my lessons in the past, whether they were really harsh or not," she said. "I just like, look, whatever comes my way I'll be ready to just face it on, and, yeah, same mindset. Nothing is going really be changing. Hopefully I can get more endorphins going for tomorrow and a bit more pumped up because it's so hot."

The strong performance comes at a crucial time in the LPGA Tour calendar. Roussin-Bouchard entered the week ranked No. 79 in the Race to the CME Globe, outside the top 60 players who earn entry into the season-ending $11 million CME Group Tour Championship. With a historic $4 million payout awaiting the winner of the finale, late-season Asian swing events like the Maybank Championship offer a vital springboard for players aiming to leapfrog into contention.

A victory on Sunday would unlock several significant achievements for Roussin-Bouchard. She would become a Rolex First-Time Winner and the fifth player to accomplish the feat this season, joining Gina Kim, Yana Wilson, Yuna Nishimura, and Yuri Yoshida. She would also become the second player from France to win on tour this season, following Celine Boutier, as well as the first French player to win the Maybank Championship. Additionally, a victory would make her the 18th unique winner on the LPGA Tour this year.

Her 54-hole position demonstrates notable progress for Roussin-Bouchard at this venue. At the 2025 event, she finished tied for 60th after recovering from a second-round 80 with a final-round 66. Now within striking distance of her first LPGA victory, she faces 18 final holes to chase down the lead and secure both her maiden title and a spot in the season-ending field.

DP World Tour Play-Offs: All you need to know
article_text:
After 40 events across 25 countries, the DP World Tour brings its 2026 season to a close across back-to-back weeks with the DP World Tour Play-Offs.

Who is involved, what is at stake and how to watch. Here, we explain all...

Introduced as part of a new-look schedule ahead of the 2024 season, the DP World Tour Play-Offs mark the concluding two events of the 2026 Race to Dubai campaign.

Following the final regular event of the season at the Genesis Championship, the top 70 available players on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World contest the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship at Yas Links.

After that, the top 50 available players will progress to the Earth course at Jumeirah Golf Estates for the season finale, the DP World Tour Championship, where the DP World Tour’s Race to Dubai champion will be crowned.

Across the DP World Tour Play-Offs, there is US$ 19 million in prize fund being played for.

Following a one-week break in the Race to Dubai, the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship will take place from Thursday, November 5th to Sunday, November 8th.

Our 13-month global odyssey comes to a close with a 42nd and final event at the DP World Tour Championship from Thursday, November 12th to Sunday, November 15th at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

An elite international field is set to gather in the capital city of the United Arab Emirates for the first of back-to-back Rolex Series events.

Aaron Rai returns for his title defence as one of six Major champions, alongside Rory McIlroy, Patrick Reed, Adam Scott, Jon Rahm and Francesco Molinari.

The top five on the Race to Dubai are all in action, with Eugenio Chacarra leading the Race to Dubai Rankings as the sole three-time winner on the DP World Tour this season.

There are nine Rolex Series winners, with Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton bidding to claim a record sixth title.

They are joined by fellow winners of the DP World Tour's blue-riband events in McIlroy, Reed, Rai, Victor Perez, Francesco Molinari, Bernd Wiesberger and Tommy Fleetwood.

Of the 70-strong field, 14 are set to make their tournament debut, including Rolex Series debutant Gregorio De Leo - one of four Qualifying School graduates.

There are 27 winners from the season in action, including Yuto Katsuragawa who only played his way into the field in style with victory at the Genesis Championship.

To view the entry list for the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship in full, click here.

The field for the DP World Tour Championship will be finalised following the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

Beginning last November and running through to August, the first phase of the season consisted of five Global Swings, before the Back 9 ran from late August through to October.

DP World Tour members have been able to win Race to Dubai points at each event, with 3,000, 3,500 or 4,000 points in the case of the Nedbank Golf Challenge in honour of Gary Player on offer within the Global Swings and an increased 5,000 points in the Back 9. At the four Major Championships, 10,000 points have been at play.

The first three Rolex Series events this season all carried 8,000 points.

To view the Race to Dubai Rankings ahead of the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, click here.

The contest to win the Race to Dubai is likely to dominate focus, with Chacarra holding the advantage as he bids to become the third Spanish winner after Rahm and Seve Ballesteros.

But in Reed and Jarvis, both two-time winners on the schedule this season, and McIlroy - Race to Dubai champion in each of the past four years and bidding to match Colin Montgomerie with a record-equalling season-long crown - he faces stiff opposition.

Players will be awarded a share of the points based on their finishing position in a tournament, with the winner in Abu Dhabi claiming 1,500 points and the champion in Dubai earning 2,000.

In addition, the winner of the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year Award will also be determined with Kota Kaneko, Michael Hollick, Stefano Mazzoli, Daniel Rodrigues and Yurav Premlall in the mix going into the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

Huge steps can also be made in discovering who wins the Seve Ballesteros Award, voted for by the Tour's own members.

Eugenio Chacarra gained an extra 51 points after his T22 at the Genesis Championship on the Race to Dubai Rankings and will head to the play-offs with a 669.27 difference ⚔️#GenesisChampionship pic.twitter.com/zvy2HYJIoP

The DP World Tour Play-Offs will be contested over 72-hole individual stroke play, with no cut.

Who has won so far on the Rolex Series in 2026?

So far on the 2026 Race to Dubai, we have seen three different players become first-time Rolex Series winners.

Will that run continue in the United Arab Emirates?

title: Stephen Larkham confirms a number of Australia A stars could link up with the Wallabies
article_text:
Stephen Larkham revealed that up to six of his Australia A squad could be playing in the Nations Championship for the Wallabies in November.

The Brumbies head coach oversaw a dominant 52-0 victory at Sports Illustrated Stadium in New Jersey on Friday, completing Australia A’s clean sweep against the USA Men.

In regular contact with Wallabies head coach Les Kiss, Larkham confirmed that several of his squad will stay on in the northern hemisphere to join up with the Test squad for the Nations Championship.

A number of the Australia A squad impressed in their 61-12 and 52-0 wins over the USA Men in Tennessee and New Jersey. Fly-half Harry McLaughlin-Phillips scored 17 points on Friday night, while cross-code star Zac Lomax was hugely impressive in his representative debut for Australia.

“This is a stepping stone for all of our players to get to that next level, which is where they all want to go,” Larkham said at Sports Illustrated Stadium.

“Some of them are in discussion at the moment – [I’ve] been back and forth with Les over the last 24 hours around some of the players before the game tonight.

“I haven’t spoken to him after the game, but we know there’s a couple of players that are going to head on the northern hemisphere tour.

“We’ve got three guys out of our squad at the moment that are going and there’s a possibility of two or three more other guys being called in.”

Larkham would not comment on which players were going to stay on in the northern hemisphere in November.

The squad touring North America includes 12 capped Wallabies, with Kiss likely to draw on that experience where needed.

After the first half of their Nations Championship campaign, Australia are currently third in the southern hemisphere pool.

In the Southern Series, the Wallabies lost narrowly to Ireland, also lost to France and got off the mark against Italy.

Kiss and the Wallabies are currently en route to the northern hemisphere for the second half of their Nations Championship campaign.

They will play England, Scotland and Wales across consecutive weekends in November before taking part in Finals Day at Allianz Stadium.

title: Carbery stars as Leinster hammer Connacht in URC
article_text:
Joey Carbery scored 20 points as Leinster hammered Connacht 50-5 in the United Rugby Championship in Galway.

Fly-half Carbery, who returned to Leinster in the summer eight years after leaving the Irish province, stared in the seven-try win.

Without their Ireland internationals ahead of the upcoming Nations Championship fictures, Leo Cullen's side made a strong start at the Dexcom Stadium as Gus McCarthy and Jordan Larmour crossed for the visitors.

Dave Heffernan got Connacht on the board in the 28th minute, but that was the last point that Stuart Lancaster's side would score.

Larmour teed up Lawlor for his first Leinster try and Carbery added his third conversion to put Leinster 21-5 to the good at half time.

Leinster picked up where they left off as Max Deegan crossed shortly after Carbery had kicked a penalty, and the former Munster and Bordeaux fly-half got in on the act with a try of his own just after the hour mark.

Ciaran Mangan got Leinster's sixth try and Fintan Gunne completed the rout when he crossed with three minutes remaining, and Carbery's conversion brought him to 20 points for the match.

Leinster move up to third in the URC table after the big win, while Connacht remain in eighth place but their nearest challengers for the final play-off place have a game in hand.

Connacht: Ioane; Bolton; Devine, Forde; Ryan; Naughton, Blade; van Wyk, Heffernan, Bealham; Murphy, O'Connor; O'Brien, Connors, Boyle.

Replacements: Victory, Cahir, Barrett, Murray, Hurley-Langton, Reilly, Treacy, Gilbert.

Leinster: Lawlor; Kenny; Fahy, Tector; Larmour; Carbery, Gunne; Usanov, McCarthy, N Smyth; Deeny, Spicer, Deegan, Penny, Culhane.

title: Study by former Trail Blazers exec reveals youth sports sponsorship advantage
López Ramírez Charges Within Two of the Lead at Maybank Championship
article_text:
Julia López Ramírez is making a serious push at the Maybank Championship. In the third round at Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club, the 23-year-old Spaniard moved up the leaderboard to 13 under par, two shots behind defending champion Miyu Yamashita. With one round left on Sunday, November 1, she is firmly in contention for the title.

The key moment came at the par-72 West Course's 7th hole. López Ramírez hit a precise wedge approach that set up a birdie, taking her to 13 under and within two of the lead. It continued a strong week for the player from Málaga. She opened with a 67, added a 66 on Friday and started the third round at 11 under, tied for fourth.

Yamashita leads at 15 under as she tries to do something nobody has done before. No player has ever successfully defended the Maybank Championship title. Last year, the Japanese star won at 18 under in a three-way playoff against Hye-Jin Choi and Hannah Green. A second straight win in Malaysia would make tournament history.

The chasing pack is tightly bunched. Australia's Robyn Choi and South Korea's A Lim Kim are at 12 under, and with the third round still being played, places on the leaderboard are changing quickly. López Ramírez is reportedly in a share of fourth, and her position may change before play finishes. The field also includes several highly ranked players, among them Ruoning Yin and Charley Hull.

The week in Kuala Lumpur fits the rapid rise of one of the LPGA Tour's most exciting young players. Born on February 11, 2003, López Ramírez was the 2023 SEC Golfer of the Year and won back-to-back SEC Women's Golf Championships in 2023 and 2024 before turning professional.

As a rookie on the LPGA Tour in 2025, she quickly became one of the circuit's best ball strikers. She finished tied third at the ISPS HANDA Women's Scottish Open and again at the BMW Ladies Championship, and tied 15th at the Ford Championship. Power is a big part of her game: she ranks first on the LPGA Tour in driving distance, averaging 288.5 yards.

That rise earned her a place on the international stage. Team Europe chose her as one of four captain's picks for the 2026 Solheim Cup, recognition of how quickly she has adapted to the top level of the women's game.

The Maybank Championship is part of the LPGA Tour's Asian Swing and has a $3.0 million prize fund. A strong finish would be another milestone for López Ramírez and could give her Rolex Rankings position a welcome boost.

Going into Sunday, the picture is clear. Yamashita is chasing history, and a group of determined challengers led by López Ramírez is close behind. If the Spaniard's wedges stay as sharp as they were at the 7th, the final round in Kuala Lumpur could be a thrilling finish.
